Theme

Money, work & business · Civic life: news, government & the law

economic adjective

also financial, economic crisis, money troubles

classical

Cic. Rosc. Am. 117: reī pecūniāriae socius (Lewis & Short)
Tac. Ann. 6.5: rēs pecūniāria (Lewis & Short)

pecūniārius, pecūniāria, pecūniārium

adjective, declension

to do with money, financial, economic

Latin has no word for the economy as a whole; it speaks of money matters, rēs pecūniāria or rēs nummāria.

Other words

  • nummārius, nummāria, nummārium — to do with money

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.2.69: difficultās nummāria, money troubles (Lewis & Short)

  • oeconomicus, oeconomica, oeconomicum — economic

    adjective, declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. minister of economic affairs (administer ab oeconomicīs negōtiīs, Egger)

    Classically of household management (Xenophon’s Oeconomicus, Cic. Off. 2.87) or of the orderly arrangement of a speech (Quint. 7.10.11); the sense of a nation’s economy is modern.

Examples

  • difficultās nummāria

    money troubles, financial difficultyCic. Verr. 2.2.69

See also money, debt, bank.
